days.title: Model and runtime
days.hook: Which model actually handled that request?
days.screen: Session-Detail mit getrennten Feldern Runtime, Provider und gemeldetem Modell; fehlenden Wert zeigen.
days.voice: An agent name and a model name describe different things. The runtime tells you which tool is managing the work. The provider and reported model describe the request behind it. O.A. - O.S keeps these fields separate. When a source does not report the model, the interface should say so. This makes a session easier to understand and a handoff easier to review. Check the source label whenever you inspect a result.
days.cta: Inspect the model and source fields in the demo.
days.tiktok: Runtime, provider, model: three useful fields for understanding AI work. Watch how O.A. - O.S separates them. #AIWorkflow #OpenSource
days.instagram: Which tool ran the session? Which provider handled it? Which model was actually reported? Keep these questions separate. Save this checklist for your AI workspace.
days.x:
Runtime, provider and reported model are different fields in O.A. - O.S. Missing data stays visibly unknown. This demo shows the distinction.
https://github.com/MasterPlayspots/O.S.-W.S.

days.title: Token numbers with context
days.hook: A token number needs a source and a time range.
days.screen: Usage-Ansicht mit Zeitraum, Quelle und reported/demo/unavailable-Kennzeichnung.
days.voice: A token total is useful when you know what it measures. Is it one request, one session or the whole project? Was it reported by the provider or shown as demo data? O.A. - O.S makes that context part of the interface. Costs also need a currency and a price basis. Missing usage is shown as unavailable. Use the demo to inspect the fields, then connect a supported event source for your own data.
days.cta: Check the usage data contract in the repository.
days.tiktok: Before comparing token totals, check the source and time range. A quick tour of usage fields in O.A. - O.S. #AITokens #DeveloperTools

days.x:

days.voice: Here is a controlled connection failure in a local test. The dashboard shows the failure and the information needed to investigate it. After correcting the test configuration, we run the check again and show the new result. That sequence matters: the status changes because of a new observation.
